s1.syndrome_frame: Facial swelling and calcified mass with a chronic time course
key_facts: 13-year-old boy
1-week history of right facial swelling and cellulitis
Noticed a mass in his right maxillary molar area 6 months earlier
Hard swelling over the right maxilla
Intraoral calcified mass
Missing right maxillary molar teeth
No sensory nerve deficits
Extensive, well-demarcated, dense amorphous irregular calcified lesion in the right maxilla
Lesion extends to the infraorbital rim

shortlist.label: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a calcified mass in the jaw

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Commonly presents as a jaw mass with calcifications

shortlist.label: Complex odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Typically presents as a calcified mass in the jaw, often associated with missing teeth

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a well-demarcated calcified lesion in the jaw

shortlist.label: Odontogenic myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause jaw swelling and may have calcified components

raw.rationale: The presence of a calcified mass, missing teeth, and a well-demarcated lesion in the maxilla is consistent with a complex odontoma, which is a type of odontogenic tumor that can cause such radiographic and clinical findings.

rejected.label: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: This tumor typically presents with a more aggressive clinical course and may have amyloid deposits, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: This tumor often presents as a well-circumscribed radiolucency, which is not consistent with the dense, calcified lesion described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: This tumor typically presents with a more aggressive clinical course and may have a softer, more fibrous component, which is not consistent with the hard, calcified mass described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Odontogenic myxoma
rejected.why: This tumor typically presents as a radiolucent lesion with a soap-bubble or honeycomb appearance, which is not consistent with the dense, calcified lesion described in the vignette.
